subject: Filtering named loci from genlight objects

messages.author: 0bfeefd4d077b98c
messages.subject: Filtering named loci from genlight objects
parts:
Hi there!

In version 1.0.5 and the version prior to 2.0.3 (I can't remember the number) of dartR I filtered named loci in the following way

#create a list of Fis =1 loci to remove
Fis1.to.remove <- match(Fis1$rowname, locNames(gl.clean))

#remove the loci from the gl and the metrics object
gl.clean_Fis1.removed <- gl.clean[, -Fis1.to.remove]
gl.clean_Fis1.removed@other$loc.metrics <- gl.clean_Fis1.removed@other$loc.metrics[-Fis1.to.remove, ]

However, in version 2.0.3 I am get the following error

Warning in View :
  data length [4324884] is not a sub-multiple or multiple of the number of rows [761]
Error in View : length of 'dimnames' [2] not equal to array extent

When I check the dimnames I find different numbers stored in the genlight object. 

dim(gl.clean_F...@n.loc) = 5683
dim(gl.clean_Fis1.removed@other$loc.metrics) = 5685 29

Any ideas what is happening here?

Many thanks,
Lana

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Filtering named loci from genlight objects
parts:
Hi Lana,

Without a reproducible example, I couldn't determine where exactly is the error. Potential sources of error could be missing data either in your genlight object or in your calculation of FIS, errors when converting to genlight object, error in previous code, etc.

Potential solutions could be filtering on missing data, call rate, monomorphic loci, running the function to check whether the genlight object is compliant and fix it if necessary. To avoid errors you could use the filter gl.filter.locmetric.

See some code example below.

library(dartR)
test <- platypus.gl
#check compliance
test <- gl.compliance.check(test)
# using only one population
test <- gl.keep.pop(test,pop.list = "TENTERFIELD")
# filtering loci with all missing data
test <- gl.filter.allna(test)
# filtering on call rate
test <- gl.filter.callrate(test,threshold = 1)
# filtering monomorphic loci
test <- gl.filter.monomorphs(test)
# calculating basic stats
stats <- utils.basic.stats(test)
# getting FIS
Fis <- stats$perloc$Fis
# assigning to loc.metrics
test$other$loc.metrics$Fis <- Fis
# filtering loci
test_removed <- gl.filter.locmetric(test, metric = "Fis", upper = 0.25, lower = min(test$other$loc.metrics$Fis), keep = "within")

Cheers,
Luis
